tasks.title: Fix the logo layout test's name check that can never fail
tasks.why: read in code: SelectionTests.cs:315-319 asserts `json.text.Contains(...) || n == "logo_full" || n == "wordmark" || n.StartsWith("glint")`. Feed it a layout.json missing `"logo_full"`, `"wordmark"`, `"glint_top_0"` or `"glint_bottom_11"` entirely: the test still reads green for those four names, so a dropped name in the shipped layout is invisible. The two `GameLogo` tests (this one and `TheLogoSpinsItsCogInThenTurnsSlowlyAndItsWordsLand`) also sit in `SelectionTests`, which `tasks.md:867` names as guarding TrenchScope/GroupAlerts/selection, not the boot logo — a reader following that row never finds them.
tasks.done_when: the four names the OR-clause currently waives are asserted with a plain Contains, and the two GameLogo tests live in a file/class tasks.md's logo row names (or tasks.md is updated to point at SelectionTests); the test goes red when layout.json is missing one of those names.

tasks.title: Share the HP-to-mood face texture rule instead of copying it twice
tasks.why: read in code: `HoverCard.SetFace` (lines 394-402: `health > 0.6f ? Mood.Neutral : health > 0.3f ? Mood.Wounded : Mood.Critical`, then `UnitArt.HasFace`/`State`/`Full`) and `SelectionPanel.RefreshHp` (lines 147-150: the identical `k > 0.6f ... > 0.3f ...` and the same three `UnitArt` calls) write the same three-tier health-to-portrait rule in two files. A future change to the thresholds or the fallback (e.g. a fourth mood tier) has to be made twice and will drift the first time someone forgets the second site.
tasks.done_when: one static helper (e.g. on UnitArt or UnitStatus) takes a health fraction and an archetype and returns the texture; both call sites use it and the mood thresholds exist in one place.

tasks.title: Make AimReadout honour CursorOverride like the rest of the input path
tasks.why: read in code: `SelectionController.HandleMouse` reads the cursor as `CursorOverride ?? mouse.position.ReadValue()` (line 206), so picking and hovering follow the override. `Tick` (lines 143-144) builds the aim readout from `mouse.position.ReadValue()` directly, never checking `CursorOverride`. Nothing in the repo sets `CursorOverride` yet (grepped, no hits besides its declaration and this one read), so it is not firing today, but it is public API clearly meant for a capture or test driver to move the simulated cursor; the first caller that sets it will see the pick/hover follow the fake point while the aim-readout card and its brackets stay glued to the real mouse.
tasks.done_when: the aim-readout call sites (SelectionController.cs:143-144) use the same `CursorOverride ?? mouse.position.ReadValue()` expression as HandleMouse; a test that sets CursorOverride and arms an ability shows the readout counted at the override point.
